simple.meaning: דֵּעָה (dêʻâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “knowledge.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across 1 Samuel, Job, Psalms, Isaiah, Jeremiah, beginning at 1 Samuel 2:3. Its contexts include kingship, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דֵּעָה (H1844).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: דֵּעָה (dêʻâh) / H1844 is traced through 1 Samuel 2:3, Job 36:4, Psalms 73:11, Isaiah 11:9 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: For truly my words are not false.
They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain;
Whom will he teach knowledge? To whom will he explain the message? Those who are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts?
I will give you shepherds according to my heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.

structuredEvidence.canonicalTrailSummary: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Samuel 2:3 and continues through Jeremiah 3:15.

definitions.full: H1844. deah דֵּעָה noun feminine knowledge (strictly Infinitive of ידע ) — דֵּעָה Psa 73:11 3 t.; plural דֵּעוֺת 1Sam 2:3 ; Job 36:4 ; — ד ׳תְּמִים 36:4 (of Elihu); of God's knowledge, ד ׳אֵל ׳י 1Sam 2:3 a God of knowledge is ׳י (on plural see Dr); בְעֶלְיוֺן דֵּעָה יֵשׁ Psa 73:11 (|| יָדַעאֵֿל אֵיכָה ); knowledge , with ׳י as object Isa 11:9 (where verbal force of noun appears); as taught by prophets 28:9 ; וְהַשְׂכֵּיל דֵּעָה אֶתְכֶם וְרָעוּ Jer 3:15 of ׳י s shepherds (i.e. future ideal rulers). Gr proposes (plausibly) רָעֹה , after ᵐ5 , see also Gie.
